key_insight: ProtoDiffusion represents a layered graphic design using one shared spatial prototype and one compact vector per layer, rather than a separate spatial grid for every layer. This offers a more compact foundation for generating multi-layer images.
problem_solved: Existing layered-image models allocate full-canvas or region-sized latent grids to individual layers, making representation size grow with their cumulative spatial extent.
method: Use ProtoVAE, a multi-layer variational autoencoder, to encode a design into a shared spatial prototype and one candidate vector per layer.
Build a latent-diffusion framework on this representation to model multi-layer images.
Represent ordered RGBA layers, whose separation supports selection, movement, and reuse.
impact: For practitioners building graphic-design tools, this approach could reduce per-layer representation overhead while retaining separately editable layers. The provided abstract is truncated, so quantitative efficiency gains and generation quality cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: Exploded stack of RGBA layers showing how they form a finished design.
Side-by-side comparison: a spatial latent grid per layer versus one shared prototype plus compact layer vectors.
Pipeline diagram: layered design → ProtoVAE encoding → latent diffusion → generated layered design.
Selection, movement, and reuse icons illustrating the value of separate layers.
paper_title: ProtoDiffusion: Token-per-Layer Generative Modeling of Multi-Layer Images
paper_authors: Adrià Ciurana Lanau, Harleen Hanspal, Lusine Abrahamyan, Emilio Tylson Baixauli, Yu Cao
